confirmed.section: §4 end-of-stage state, §8 seated branch, §8.5 asymmetry, §11 blat-copy
confirmed.contract: Carve-resolved grid cells hold real tile bytes; the 0x5C seated branch fires when the visibility-grid byte is chair 0x92 and stamps the actor's own frame (no variant draw); shipped 0x5C NPCs take this arm on their 0x92 waypoints.
confirmed.evidence: The viewport render path (chunk_09.rs:611-617) uses the visibility buffers. rebuild_top_down_visibility_buffers (chunk_09.rs:1541-1542) and copy_combat_terrain_to_visibility_buffers (chunk_09.rs:1576-1581) write terrain only into terrain_band. A 0x5C actor on a 0x92 chair therefore goes to the default helper with frame-8 and gets the 0x92 row result: 0x32, or 0x34..0x37 with a shared-stream draw (visibility.rs:397). The prepare_top_down_render_grid path does put terrain in grid (chunk_09.rs:1872-1875), but it serves only queries and the text view, not the main viewport.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Make the producer and blat-copy leave real terrain bytes in the grid for carve-resolved cells, as §4 says, and let fog/markers apply as published. Either way, add a test that a 0x5C slot on 0x92 stamps its own frame and takes no draw.

confirmed.contract: On a clean frame each 0x00 grid cell is refilled by writing the world-tile getter's byte into the visibility grid. The cell becomes a direct terrain tile and is no longer a use-companion cell.
confirmed.evidence: lazy_refill_top_down_visibility_buffers (chunk_09.rs:1548-1570) writes the fetched terrain into terrain_band[terrain_index] and leaves visibility_grid at 0x00. PreparedTopDownCell::tile_id (chunk_09.rs:35-37) paints a UseCompanion cell as actor_tile_for_byte(terrain) = 0x100+terrain (tile_helpers.rs:1888), so a refilled terrain byte is drawn from the actor bank. The water-bound arm then skips a cell already at 0x00 (visibility.rs:451-453), so a stationary 0xE8..0xEB/0x1E/0x1F slot is not restamped: its cell shows the refilled terrain id from the second bank. In the spec, the grid byte becomes nonzero, so the slot restamps. Separately, visibility.md §9 says the renderer paints direct bytes through the animated-tile table.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In the lazy refill, write the fetched tile byte into visibility_grid (a direct tile) instead of terrain_band, matching §10. Then the renderer's DirectTile arm paints it from the first bank, and the water-bound guard sees a nonzero byte and restamps.

With this loop, monsters whose frame byte is in 0xB0..0xB3/0xBC..0xBF/0xDC/0xDE emit a 37-cell light.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Delete the active_objects loop from rebuild_surface_local_light_mask so the mask is built from map-window terrain only. Add a test that a Dragon/Insect-Swarm-frame actor lights nothing.

confirmed.contract: Each successful surface/town chest row acquires a free active-object slot (downward scan; index 0 means none) and stages family+quantity there as a floor object for a later Get. If no slot is free, the row is dropped silently.
confirmed.evidence: generate_surface_object_chest_content (chunk_06.rs:1237-1360) calls apply_object_pickup directly for each successful primary row (lines 1253, 1258, 1263, 1268, 1281, 1294, 1302) and for equipment (line 1350). It allocates no slot, stages no floor object, and has no drop-when-full handling. The chest-marker row (1306-1321) stages nothing. No slot-allocator helper is called anywhere on this path (grep found none).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add a shared downward free-slot allocator that treats a returned index 0 as none. For each successful row, write the family/quantity into the slot at the chest coordinate instead of crediting inventory, and print the family line only when staging succeeds. Let the existing Get object path perform the transfer.

confirmed.contract: Gate (1..30), quantity and equipment-index (0..47) rolls come from the shared random helper. Gold and Chest-marker take a discarded first draw (1..90 / 1..10) before the family roll. An ineligible equipment index skips its 1..30 draw.
confirmed.evidence: Every roll goes through surface_object_chest_roll / surface_object_chest_zero_based_roll, which wrap surface_object_chest_seed (chunk_06.rs:1362-1412). That seed is an XOR hash of turn/slot/x/y/class/row/stage, and the shared gameplay PRNG is never advanced. The Gold row (1297-1305) and marker row (1306-1321) make no discarded first draw. The equipment loop (1340-1348) draws the 1..30 roll for any non-disabled row, and only chest_primary_pool_row_succeeds then tests threshold <= class. So ineligible indices still draw.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Replace the hash with self.random_range_u8 (the shared helper) in the published order. Add the discarded 1..90 draw for Gold and the 1..10 draw for Chest-marker. In the equipment loop, test threshold <= class before drawing the 1..30 roll.

confirmed.contract: Generator inputs are depth, the underfoot cell byte with its low nibble discarded, fixed tables, and the shared random helper. X/Y only index the cell, and nothing per-coordinate influences the contents.
confirmed.evidence: generate_dungeon_chest_content (chunk_07.rs:619+) draws every gate and quantity roll from dungeon_chest_roll_seed (chunk_07.rs:790-806). That seed is turn ^ hour*3 ^ minute*5 ^ level*17 ^ x*19 ^ y*23 ^ tile*29 ^ row*31 ^ stage*37, so coordinates and the tile byte feed content generation and the shared PRNG is not consumed. This contradicts the explicit negative in §6 ('Nothing per-chest, per-room, per-level or per-coordinate is consulted').
confirmed.fix_sketch: Drive the row gate (1..4*depth+4) and the quantity rolls from the shared random helper. Remove x/y/tile/clock from the roll inputs, keeping the depth-0 gold 1..0 edge as §6 specifies.

confirmed.contract: The detection threshold uses slot difficulty and the acting member's Intelligence. The acting member comes from the shared acting-member selection, and the roll is a uniform 1..30 draw.

confirmed.fix_sketch: Route through the shared acting-member selector (traps.md §2.1 priority, including the None! abort). Pass that member's Intelligence to search_trap_detection_threshold, and take the 1..30 roll from the shared random helper.

confirmed.section: 7 (No dungeon arm writes the active-object table; X-it's dungeon scene test is dead code) / 5.8 `X` on foot

confirmed.contract: The spawner rejects a candidate only for separation, zero bucket, sea creature on shore, and the 128 cap. There is no occupancy test; a full table is handled by eviction.
confirmed.evidence: play_state_impl/chunk_09.rs:177-182 also rejects any candidate where self.world_object_at(x, y).is_some(). §4 lists the retry steps exhaustively, and §9 (encounters.md:739-751) says the only silent no-spawn is the 128-candidate cap. The extra test changes which candidates are accepted and how many random draws a spawn uses.

confirmed.contract: A delivered shipwright Frigate is placed with hull condition 99 in byte +5 (100 retracted) and two skiffs in byte +7.

confirmed.section: §4 B-Board boardable object bytes table / 'What?' fallthrough
confirmed.contract: Only object bytes 0x10..0x11, 0x1B, 0x24..0x27 and 0x28..0x2B are boardable. Anything else gets 'What?'.
confirmed.evidence: tile_helpers.rs:675-687: when boardable_family(type_byte) is None, transport_from_vehicle_object falls back to the record's tile byte (record[1]) and maps 160..167, 168..175, 176..183 and 184..187 to Horse/Ship/Skiff/Carpet. confirmed.section: §4 B-Board ('reads the vehicle or object under the party'; 'probes the current position')
confirmed.contract: B-Board looks for a boardable object only at the party's current position.
confirmed.evidence: play_state_impl/chunk_10.rs:150-170: board_probe_positions returns the party cell plus the facing-adjacent cell on the world and in towns. boardable_vehicle_slot (chunk_10.rs:115-120) takes the first hit, so a vehicle in the facing cell can be boarded. No spec text allows an adjacent probe.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Have board_probe_positions (or boardable_vehicle_slot) probe only (player.x, player.y), and update the tests that rely on adjacent boarding.

confirmed.contract: A furled-ship exit onto land, into the carried skiff, or onto a stowed carpet shows only 'X-it ship!' with no further success text.
confirmed.evidence: play_state_impl/chunk_07.rs:1243-1245: the land-exit success path builds format!("{}!", kind_name) and then calls transport.append_ship_auxiliary_warnings (transport.rs:593-606). That appends ' DANGER: SHIP BADLY DAMAGED!' when hull < 10 and ' WARNING: NO SKIFFS ON BOARD!' when skiffs == 0. Those are boarding-only warnings in §4. The skiff and carpet fallback paths (chunk_07.rs:1151/1180) are correct.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Remove the append_ship_auxiliary_warnings call from the X-it success path, so the line is just the completed 'X-it <kind>!' echo.

confirmed.contract: Under sail, X-it prints 'X-it_\nUnder sail!\n': the refusal goes on its own row below the echo.
confirmed.evidence:
chunk_07.rs:1091 sets message = SHIP_XIT_UNDER_SAIL_REFUSAL = "Under sail!" (commands.rs:856), with no leading or trailing line feed. X-it is an AwaitsArgument echo (commands.rs:1192, 'X-it '), and success words such as 'horse!' rely on continuing that open row. The sibling refusals carry explicit feeds: XIT_NO_LAND_NEARBY_REFUSAL "
No land nearby!
" (commands.rs:896) and the bridge "
Not here!
" (chunk_07.rs:1219). The spec gives '
Under sail!
' in both the §5.1 table and 'Sailing feedback'. I did not run it, but the code has no mechanism that would supply the leading feed.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Change SHIP_XIT_UNDER_SAIL_REFUSAL to "\nUnder sail!\n", or emit it the way XIT_NO_LAND_NEARBY_REFUSAL is emitted, so it lands on a new row under 'X-it '.

confirmed.contract: Vehicle directional steps announce 'Ride'/'Fly'/'Row' + direction. A frigate gets no prefix in towns, and a frigate turning in place on the overworld announces 'Head'.
confirmed.evidence: commands.rs:1950-1966: movement_echo(direction) returns only the bare compass word. message_transcript.rs:942-951: top_down_command_echo(key) uses it with no transport input, called from play_state_impl/chunk_02.rs:337. None of the crates has a Ride/Fly/Row/Head echo literal; the only mention is the comment at chunk_05.rs:1008. u5-bevy and u5-tui add no prefix either.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Pass the current transport (and whether the frigate step is a turn in place, and the scene) into the movement echo, and prepend 'Ride '/'Fly '/'Row ', or 'Head ' for an overworld frigate turn, before the compass word.

confirmed.contract: The broadside runs the shared pre-action gate, animates the impact on a hit, and animates the projectile to the endpoint on a miss. No engineering report.
confirmed.evidence: play_state_impl/chunk_07.rs:2709-2769 fire_ship_broadside is the only world F-Fire path (dispatched at chunk_07.rs:2534). It has no pre-action gate call and no projectile or impact presentation. It writes debug text: 'BOOOM! Ship broadside hit object tile {} at ({}, {}) for {damage} durability damage; ...', '... fired {dir} with no target in range.', and 'Fire- which direction? Use F plus a direction in this harness.' No MoveOutcome::Fired consumer animates a shot.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add the shared pre-action gate before the facing test. Replace the debug strings with a projectile presentation along the up-to-three-cell line that ends with an impact on a hit or at the endpoint on a miss, routed through the existing projectile/impact presentation used by ranged attacks.

confirmed.section: §5 'One family, named, with its gate arithmetic' (beggar 364..367)
confirmed.contract: The beggar family 0x6C..0x6F steps base->1->2->3. From the third frame it re-bases on a 1-in-4 roll and holds base for six ticks; otherwise it rewinds to the first frame. Every decision is behind a fair coin.
confirmed.evidence: tile_helpers.rs:819-869: active_object_frame_family gives every type byte 0x40..0xBF a plain 4-frame family, and active_object_next_frame_tile does +1 mod 4. animate_active_object_decision_point (play_state_impl/chunk_09.rs:4636-4650) applies that after the fair coin (4655-4657), so a beggar cycles 6C->6D->6E->6F->6C. It never rewinds to 6D, has no 1-in-4 re-base and no six-tick hold. The script exists only for the shrine kneeling pose (shrine_presentation.rs tick_kneeling_frame, called at chunk_09.rs:4392). Town NPCs are active objects animated by this same pass.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In the decision-point animator, special-case type bytes 0x6C..0x6F to reuse the shrine kneeling script: from the third frame draw value%256 < 64 to re-base and hold six ticks, else rewind to the first frame; keep the fair coin. Share the code with shrine_presentation.

confirmed.section: §13.2 (third gating state; 'the very first world step of a session is a bare repaint')
confirmed.contract: The gating byte starts in a freeze state, so the first world step of a session skips object animation and the tile passes.
confirmed.evidence: I found no initial-freeze flag. AnimationAssetBuffer::AT_BOOT (animation.rs:268-274) only zeroes the clocks. advance_visual_tick_inner (chunk_09.rs:3831ff) runs animate_active_objects and advance_animation_clock on the very first call. Grepping for 'first world step', 'bare repaint', 'freeze state', 'tandy' and 'gating byte' finds only unrelated hits. The first step therefore takes animator fair-coin PRNG draws that the spec says are skipped. The spec does not say whether 'the freeze state' means a full skip state or the Tandy sentinel, so whether the wind check also skips on that step is open. Under both readings, object animation and both tile passes are skipped, and the engine skips none of them.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add a session-start latch (set at program/session start, cleared after one world step) that makes the first advance_visual_tick skip animate_active_objects and advance_animation_clock while still repainting. Ask the spec owner whether the wind check and ambience tick are skipped too.

confirmed.contract: 0x83 is a timed pause of up to 28 non-blocking redraw/poll passes, ended and consumed by a key or by the 28th pass. 0x8F blocks for one keystroke and emits nothing. Both apply on every response path.
confirmed.evidence: Spec lines 401-404 (R520, corrected 2026-10-12) settle the contract. Every caller hard-codes yield_on_pause:false: conversation_session.rs:877, chunk_04.rs:4643 and 5004. As a result tlk_runner.rs:491-508 only pushes PauseSkipped for 0x83 (no consumer anywhere in crates/) and emits a '\n' glyph for 0x8F (WaitKeyTreatedAsNewline). The comment at conversation_session.rs:860-876 defers to #284, which R520 has since resolved.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Turn on yield_on_pause in make_inputs. Handle PausedAt in the session/PlayState as a resumable state that resumes after 28 frame-redraw ticks or on a consumed key, then flushes type-ahead. Handle WaitingKey as a blocking one-key wait that emits no glyph.

confirmed.contract: A GOTO/taken IF-ELSE rewinds to the start of the blob, finds the two-byte declaration 0x90 <label>, and resumes just past it, running the labelled record's text and controls.
confirmed.evidence: map_io.rs:36-66 splits each blob into fields at every NUL, and the spec says shipped declarations always follow a NUL. tlk_runner.rs:797-818 find_label_position_excluding scans only the current field and matches the bare label byte, with no 0x90 prefix check. A target in another record therefore gives UnresolvedGotoLabel (tlk_runner.rs:634/673), which absorb_run (conversation_session.rs:626-637) drops through `_ => {}`, so the response ends silently. A plain GOTO only stops with LabelTransfer (tlk_runner.rs:680), and the session merely switches to AwaitingScopedKeyword (conversation_session.rs:631-634/742) without executing the labelled record's own bytes.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Keep a whole-blob byte view (or a field-offset map) in ConversationSession. On a GOTO or IF-ELSE transfer, scan the whole blob for 0x90,label and continue run_tlk_stream_from at that position. The scoped prompt should then open only when that record's stream reaches its prompt.

confirmed.contract: Only the first occurrence of each member's 4-char prefix is tested. If it is mid-word, that member is abandoned even when a clean hit follows later.
confirmed.evidence: tlk_control_codes.rs:444-447 uses `folded.windows(prefix_len).enumerate().any(|(at, w)| (at==0 || folded[at-1]==b' ') && w==prefix)`, which accepts any qualifying later occurrence. The function's doc comment quotes older text ('the scan continues') that lacks the current first-occurrence-only sentence (spec lines 519-526).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Use `position()` to find the first window equal to the prefix, then accept only if that index is 0 or follows a space. Otherwise continue to the next slot.

confirmed.contract: An empty line at the ASK-WHO prompt prints the dismissive acknowledgement and returns to the stream. It never echoes or prints BYE.
confirmed.evidence: The session layer itself is correct (conversation_session.rs:329-366 routes AwaitingAskWho to the dismissive arm). The PlayState wrapper is not: chunk_04.rs:5300-5308 computes empty_line from line.trim() regardless of phase and commits the TLK_EMPTY_INPUT_BYE_ECHO onto the open ':' row (open_prompt_line, chunk_03.rs:590, returns the ASK-WHO ':' row). It then strips `spent` leading glyphs from the rendered acknowledgement at chunk_04.rs:5313-5323 even though it does not start with BYE.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In submit_active_conversation_keyword, gate the BYE echo and the leading-byte strip on the session being in AwaitingKeyword (not AwaitingAskWho or scoped phases), e.g. `empty_line && !session.awaiting_ask_party_name()`.

confirmed.section: 2 step 5 guard gate / decision tree (behaviour-4 rewrite)
confirmed.contract: If the reached waypoint's behaviour is 4, the dispatcher rewrites it to 1 (persisted, in the save) before dispatch. This applies to shopkeepers and to the automatic-contact path too.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_04.rs:4304-4318 (and the raw path near 4527) only reads the AI byte to skip the guard refusal. The only writers of the schedule AI bytes are town_npc_mutations.rs:38 and npc_runtime.rs:876/893 (forced pursuit/flight fill). No talk or contact code writes behaviour 1 to schedule[NPC_SCHEDULE_AI_OFFSET+cached_wp]. The doc comment at chunk_04.rs:4049-4053 acknowledges the rewrite is not implemented.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In a shared dispatcher prelude used by explicit Talk, shop entry and automatic contact, run before the shop and guard gates: if npc_ai_behavior(schedule[AI+cached_wp]) is approach-and-converse, set it to 1 and record_town_npc_mutation so it persists in the save.

confirmed.contract: Index 0xFD prints, after the leading LF: '"', then 'Don't hurt me!' ⏎ 'Please go away!', then '"' and an LF.
confirmed.evidence: town_mode.rs:516-518 has TOWN_NPC_COWERING_DIALOG_ID=0xFD and TOWN_NPC_COWERING_RESPONSE="They cower in fear.". It is used at chunk_04.rs:5069 and 5756. A grep of the whole worktree finds no 'hurt me' or 'Please go away' anywhere.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Replace the constant with the published rows, framed as LF, '"', "Don't hurt me!\nPlease go away!", '"', LF, and emit it from both call sites.

confirmed.contract: The rebuke prints its line with reserved-response quote/newline framing, then runs a bounded pause loop (at most 28 passes, key-abort) before returning to the keyword prompt.
confirmed.evidence: conversation_session.rs:396-398 calls out.set_plain_text(TLK_RESERVED_REBUKE_MESSAGE) (no quote framing; the constant at tlk_control_codes.rs:786-787 is the bare text plus \n\n). TLK_RESERVED_REBUKE_PAUSE_LIMIT (tlk_control_codes.rs:788) is only re-exported (lib.rs:926) and never consumed, so no pause runs.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Use set_framed_text (or the shared reserved-response framing) for the rebuke, and return a pause request with limit 28 that uses the same timed-pause mechanism as 0x83 before reissuing the prompt.

confirmed.contract: When the faced active object has no occupied, non-idle NPC record, Talk runs the dispatcher on an all-zero record and prints the bare 'No response!' rather than 'Nobody's here!'.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_04.rs:4150-4176 talk_target_in_direction resolves only through npc_at_current_floor (chunk_10.rs:382-391, which looks only at the npcs list) and never consults active_objects/object_at_current_floor. A faced object with no NPC record therefore falls through to TALK_NOBODY_HERE_LINE at chunk_04.rs:4222-4223 and 4451-4453.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In talk_target_in_direction, when no NPC is found but blocking_object_at(x,y) is an occupied object, return a target with dialog_id 0 so the dispatcher's zero-word arm prints the bare 'No response!' (the dispatcher variant, without the mirror-string LF).

confirmed.contract: Every counter letter A..G and K, including F, adds one per 0x86 call via the capped-add helper (cap 99) and never assigns a fixed value.
confirmed.evidence: Spec lines 779 and 785 give F as '+1 (cap 99)' with no fixed-value assignment. chunk_04.rs:4888-4890 does `self.climbing_gear = 1` for SetGrappleGate, and the legacy apply_talk_action_grants (chunk_04.rs ~5721) does the same, so repeated F grants stick at 1.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Change both arms to `self.climbing_gear = self.climbing_gear.saturating_add(1).min(PARTY_BYTE_STOCK_CAP)`.

confirmed.contract: Only a truly empty line takes the BYE shortcut. A line of a single space is not empty, runs the normal scan, and ends in the no-match line.
confirmed.evidence: input.md section 8 accepts space as printable input, and conversation.md line 528 states a lone space is not empty. The engine trims everywhere: input_dispatch.rs:4211-4216 drops a ' ' key and calls line.trim(); chunk_04.rs:5300 tests line.trim().is_empty(); and conversation_session.rs:882-889 capped_tlk_input_bytes trims before the empty/kind test. A typed single space therefore becomes EmptyByeShortcut and closes the conversation (and becomes an empty ASK-WHO answer).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Keep the raw typed bytes (capped to 15) and test emptiness on length only. Stop trimming in input_dispatch, chunk_04 and capped_tlk_input_bytes; the keyword compare already handles boundaries.

confirmed.contract: Each subtitle-ignition publication waits 45 (sounded) or 50 (silent) driver-local calibrated units. At the normative 0.88 ms ±10% anchor (driver unit about 0.92 ms) that is about 41 and 46 ms. The 14 ms modernised cadence is scoped to the TITLE.BIT flourish only.
confirmed.evidence: timing.md 5.1 limits the 14 ms normative cadence to the flourish (lines 190-230). The ignition row (line 142) and the 6.3 table (lines 382-383) give 45/50 units, and 7.1 makes 0.79-0.97 ms per unit normative, i.e. 35.6-48.5 ms per publication. u5-bevy/src/lib.rs:503 sets INTRO_SUBTITLE_IGNITION_SILENT_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_SECS=0.014 and lib.rs:11311-11313 scales by units/50, giving 14 ms and 12.6 ms. That is outside the band, about 3x too fast.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Derive the interval from the calibrated-unit anchor: wait_units * UNIT_SECS with UNIT_SECS in 0.00079..0.00097 (e.g. 0.00088 or the 0.00092 driver-local figure), giving about 0.044 s for 50 units and 0.040 s for 45.

confirmed.contract: 0x0D pauses for a keypress and then resumes printing. The high bit selects a text-output presentation mode the renderer must honour.
confirmed.evidence: The pause half is concrete and missing. signs_io.rs:280-294 decode_sign_payload maps 0x0D to '\n' with no wait, and the module doc at signs_io.rs:9 admits the pause becomes a paragraph break. The flat String body is joined by chunk_04.rs:3903-3907 into one message, so nothing downstream can pause. SignBodyByteKind::PauseForKey (signs_io.rs:60/106) is classified but has no production consumer. The high-bit 'presentation mode' half is underspecified (the spec never says what the mode does), so the gap rests on the 0x0D pause.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Decode sign bodies into segments split at 0x0D (and carry the high-bit flag per glyph), and have the Look/sign message path present each segment followed by a blocking any-key wait before continuing.

confirmed.contract: The only name check is that each of the first eight bytes is NUL or >= 0x20, so bytes >= 0x7F and blank names pass and are imported. Only a typed replacement name is refused when blank.
confirmed.evidence: The preview (u4_transfer_preview.rs:803-811) applies exactly the spec gate. The commit path apply_u4_transfer_to_save (u4_transfer.rs:236-240) calls normalize_u4_transfer_name (u4_transfer.rs:303-335), which returns InvalidNameByte for any byte outside 0x20..=0x7E and BlankName for an all-space or empty name. A source the preview accepts then fails at commit, and no save is written (u4_transfer.rs:292-293). Spec section 7's name row is 'copy up to eight characters'; the blank refusal exists only in the Name-replace stage (line 539).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Make normalize_u4_transfer_name copy bytes verbatim up to NUL/8 with only the spec's <0x20 control rejection. Move the BlankName check to the typed Name-replace input, not the imported source name.

confirmed.section: §6 Three-digit hulls run past the field; §2.1 The one arm that does request a scroll
confirmed.contract: Ship-variant counters row is unclamped: hull >= 100 writes column 39, wraps the stats cursor, and the date row's leading feed requests a strip scroll that lifts message history by one row on every repaint (non-combat, ship marker, hull >= 100).
confirmed.evidence: crates/u5-runtime/src/stats_panel.rs:1607-1621 builds `Ship:{hull}` and passes it through fixed_panel_line (l.1674), which truncates to STATS_PANEL_WIDTH (15). The painter at stats_panel.rs:1333-1338 emits `line.trim_end().bytes().take(STATS_PANEL_WIDTH)`, so column 39 is never written. MessageLog::scroll_strip (message_window.rs:220) exists, but its only callers are tests (message_window.rs:1197, 1221). The only live strip-scroll producer is the item picker (chunk_04.rs:460). Nothing in repaint_stats_panel (chunk_03.rs:431) or the painter tests hull >= 100. TransportState::Ship hull is a u8, so values up to 255 are representable. The spec states that reachability in stock play is open, but the behaviour is a contract wherever the byte holds 100 or more.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In render_stats_panel_counter_row, do not truncate the ship variant: keep the third hull digit at column 39. In repaint_stats_panel (or the painter), when not in combat, the marker is in the ship family and hull >= 100, call MessageLog::scroll_strip once per repaint so painted message rows lift by one while the write position stays put.

confirmed.section: §2.2.1 immediate-site table (U-Use after pick, Stats browser exit, R Ready end, dungeon post-action redraw, combat entry/exit) with §2.4 wishing-well staleness
confirmed.contract: Immediate sites repaint the whole panel unconditionally from live state, so a panel left stale by a no-refresh path (wishing-well debit) is corrected by the next such repaint even when that command changed no counter.
confirmed.evidence: input_dispatch.rs:31-32 snapshots live state as the baseline at command start. input_dispatch.rs:79-85 repaints only when the live snapshot differs from that baseline, so a command that changes no counter never refreshes the stale `state.stats_panel`. The comment at l.73-77 says this test exists to keep the well debit hidden, which over-applies §2.4: §2.4 says 'any inline repaint' reveals it. The only assignments to state.stats_panel are repaint_stats_panel (chunk_03.rs:432) and drain (chunk_03.rs:447). Unconditional callers are the constructors (chunk_01.rs:1033/1392/1805, which are boot paint only), the town hazard (chunk_07.rs:3716), Blackthorn (chunk_07.rs:5493) and bevy fixtures. I found none at Z-stats exit, U-Use pick, R-Ready end, dungeon post-action redraw or combat entry/exit.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add explicit unconditional state.repaint_stats_panel() calls at the immediate sites §2.2.1 lists as 'whole panel': U-Use right after item pick, Stats browser exit, R Ready end, dungeon post-action redraw, combat entry and exit. Alternatively, let those handlers mark the command as an unconditional repaint that bypasses the baseline-diff test.

confirmed.section: §2.2.1 deferred row 13 with §2.2 'A raise does not depend on the change surviving'
confirmed.contract: The combat Escape key raises the deferred refresh request on both the refused and the accepted outcome.
confirmed.evidence: combat_frame.rs:7622-7629: apply_combat_escape_cleanup returns CombatEscapeCleanupApplication::refused before setting PanelRefreshMode::Deferred. Even when Deferred is set, input_dispatch.rs:79 only raises the request if a counter changed, so a refusal (no change) never raises. The difference shows only when the panel is already stale, for example after a wishing-well debit, where the spec would repaint at the next combat prompt.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Call state.request_stats_panel_refresh() directly (not via the diff-gated command mode) at the top of the Escape handler, before the accepted or refused decision, so both outcomes raise the request regardless of whether any counter changed.

confirmed.section: §10.2 Overworld gate on the prompt pair (R497)
confirmed.contract: Overworld prompt pair (leading line feed plus end-cap) is suppressed for exactly one prompt after any direction taken aboard a ship (repeat or turn). The flag is re-armed after the test, set unconditionally on overworld entry, and never touched on foot.
confirmed.evidence: message_window.rs:493-499 calls log.end_turn() for every command echo unless entry.continues_open_row is set. continues_open_row comes only from the combat banner (message_transcript.rs:385) and surface_command_row_follows_history (message_transcript.rs:754), which is set only at shrine sites (chunk_02.rs:1994, 2102). The derived-row exceptions at message_window.rs:575-598 cover the view overlay, surface prompts and the mixer, with no ship term. The shipboard direction paths (resolve_sailed_ship_wind_gate, chunk_06.rs:196-230; movement_echo, commands.rs:1950; under-sail swallow, input_dispatch.rs:244) set no prompt-suppression state. A grep for transport/sail checks in message_window.rs and message_transcript.rs finds none.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add a PlayState flag `overworld_prompt_pair_armed`, set on every overworld entry. Clear it in the world move dispatcher whenever a direction is taken while the transport is a ship (both the turn and the repeat arms of resolve_sailed_ship_wind_gate, plus synthesized under-sail moves). When rendering the next overworld command echo, skip end_turn and the marker if the flag is clear, then re-arm it.

confirmed.contract: Record 13 sets no found-bitmap bit and has no persistence of its own; it stages whenever keys==0 and no NPC is on the tile; spending every key re-opens it.
confirmed.evidence: crates/u5-runtime/src/play_state_impl/chunk_06.rs:2638-2642 KeyNpcGated also requires !fixed_hidden_treasure_found(entry.record); chunk_06.rs:2663-2673 mark_fixed_hidden_treasure_found's `_ =>` arm calls set_fixed_hidden_treasure_found for KeyNpcGated. Spec §2 (line 22-29) says none of records 13/14/15 sets a found-bitmap bit, and record 13's only gate is the Keys counter plus NPC test.

confirmed.contract: The overworld Klimb handler's value is not forwarded, so its gear and on-foot refusals still report 'acted' and cost the outdoor turn.

confirmed.contract: Every resolved non-dungeon Open attempt returns committed-action status, including already-open, too-heavy, locked, and generic refusal paths.

(town) and 274-275 (overworld) return Blocked with no advance. Only 'It's open!'/'Too heavy!'/'Opened!' call advance_turn_without_door_tick (294, 299, 329). confirmed.section: §8 directed step planner / random fallback; §3 byte 6 (R340)
confirmed.contract: If neither directed axis is accepted, the slot falls back to a random four-direction walker rolling one cardinal direction for one attempt; byte 6 carries no facing.
confirmed.evidence: Spec §8 lines 684-688 and §3 lines 49, 93. Engine chunk_09.rs:5455-5462 takes the fallback direction from direction_from_active_object_phase(object.phase) (tile_helpers.rs:883, byte-6 high nibble) with no random roll; chunk_09.rs:5575-5576 writes active_object_phase_from_direction(direction, ...) (tile_helpers.rs:897) into byte 6 on every committed step, so byte 6 carries a facing and the fallback repeats the last step.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Replace the phase-derived fallback with a random roll of one of four cardinals (shared RNG) and one try_step attempt; stop writing a direction into the phase high nibble in try_step_outdoor_active_object_detail.

confirmed.contract: A 0xFC slot at a listed wrapped (dy,dx) mask cell increments its first aux byte as an age counter and requests a directed step only while that counter is below 20.
confirmed.evidence: Spec §8 lines 656-675. fc_sprite_proximity_mask_hits (view_classes.rs:18, re-exported lib.rs:1008) and FC_PROXIMITY_AGE_CAP (active_object_io.rs:104) have no non-test callers; advance_outdoor_active_objects (chunk_09.rs:4659-4740) and try_wander_active_object_with_last_vacated (chunk_09.rs:5423-5463) have no 0xFC branch and never touch aux1.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In the movement-dispatch step for a slot whose type is 0xFC, compute wrapped |dy|,|dx|; if fc_sprite_proximity_mask_hits, increment aux1 and only call the directed planner while aux1 < FC_PROXIMITY_AGE_CAP (else no step); otherwise fall through to ordinary directed movement.

confirmed.contract: Whirlpool-class slots flip a stored parity bit each turn and move only on turns where it clears, choosing between a random cardinal step and the directed planner.
confirmed.evidence: Spec §8 lines 622-628 and correction 645-647. advance_outdoor_active_objects (chunk_09.rs:4659-4740) only special-cases wind-driven ships; its comment at 4712 claims the whirlpool parity is 'inside the committer', but try_step_outdoor_active_object_detail (chunk_09.rs:5521-5580) has no whirlpool or parity logic. No non-comment whirlpool parity code exists anywhere in play_state_impl.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Before the directed planner, for is_whirlpool_object slots toggle a persisted parity bit (in an aux byte) and skip movement on the set phase; on the clear phase choose (by RNG) between a random cardinal attempt and the directed planner.

confirmed.section: §8 outdoor walker predicate / terrain-combat class table
confirmed.contract: 0xB4..0xB7 and 0xE8..0xEB subfamilies do not reach the generic adjacent fallback through the ordinary walker; classification reads byte 0.

confirmed.contract: Save game? accepts only Y and N; on N it prints `No` and returns.

Engine chunk_03.rs:3174 matches 'N' | '\u{1b}' for every kind except TrollBridgeToll, so Escape declines SaveGame; the SaveGame decline falls to the else arm at chunk_03.rs:3197-3199 printing "No."; chunk_01.rs:177-179 save_game_command(Some(false)) also prints "No.". confirmed.contract: The per-frame slot-zero refresh writes bytes 0..4 only (while scene < 0x80); bytes 5, 6, 7 round-trip untouched.

Engine chunk_10.rs:42-104 sync_player_object computes aux1/aux3 from transport (hull/skiffs on a ship, 0 otherwise) and writes active_objects[0].aux1 and aux3 (lines 95-96) on every call. confirmed.contract: Open treats only exact tile 0xAF as already open; an opened door cell is the ordinary cleared tile 0x44, not an already-open selector.
confirmed.evidence: Spec §2 lines 28-37 (Open writes 0x44, and 'Open alone treats exact tile 0xAF as already open'). No spec text grants 0x44 an already-open meaning. Engine chunk_06.rs:290-297 also prints "It's open!" when tile == TOWN_DOOR_CLEARED_TILE (0x44) and is_recorded_open_town_door holds, using an engine-only open-door list (record_open_town_door at 327, forget_open_town_door at chunk_10.rs:34).

confirmed.contract: AI 3/6 act only while party Manhattan distance from NPC < 4; AI 4 chooses wander/engage only from party-to-waypoint distance (< 4 engages).
confirmed.evidence: Spec §9 'The engagement step': 'Values 3/6 use a Manhattan distance strictly below four from the NPC's current position to the party.' Engine crates/u5-runtime/src/play_state_impl/chunk_10.rs:1765 `TOWN_NPC_CHASE_RADIUS: usize = 8`; flee gate at :843 and AI 6 (and AI 4 engage arm) gate at :886-891 use `<= TOWN_NPC_CHASE_RADIUS`. engages_without_distance_gate (npc_runtime.rs:477) covers only 5/7, so AI 4's engage arm takes an extra NPC-to-party <=8 gate on top of the waypoint test at :862-864.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Replace the radius constant with a strict `< 4` NPC-to-party test for AI 3/6, and drop the NPC-to-party gate from the AI 4 engage arm so that only the waypoint-distance test at chunk_10.rs:862 decides.

confirmed.contract: An approaching NPC tests legal orthogonal neighbours in E,N,W,S order and takes the first that strictly reduces Manhattan distance to the party. Modes 5/7 add random direction variation.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:1281-1305 town_npc_chase_step tries the larger-|d| axis and then the other axis, not a first-fit E,N,W,S scan. Example: dx=+1, dy=-5 steps north, where the spec steps east. Modes 5/7 use the same deterministic step (chunk_10.rs:886-898), and the runtime has no random-redirection draw. The variation's rate is unpublished, but the E,N,W,S order is concrete.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Rewrite town_npc_chase_step to iterate [East, North, West, South] and take the first legal neighbour whose Manhattan distance to the party is strictly smaller. Add the 5/7 random variation once the spec publishes its rate, or flag that rate as a spec gap.

confirmed.contract: The per-step cell check refuses any cell occupied by another active object or the party, with no distance cutoff. Only the workspace builder applies the <4-from-destination cutoff.
confirmed.evidence: Spec §10: 'the per-step gate applies no cutoff'. chunk_11.rs:161-203 npc_can_step_toward refuses an occupied cell only when npc_dynamic_obstacle_blocks(occupant, destination) holds. That function is used for direct steps (chunk_10.rs:1018), replay (:1228), wander/chase (:1411, :1436, :1457) and also as the BFS predicate (:1494). No separate cutoff-free occupancy check exists. The party cell itself is refused unconditionally (:180), so only NPC-on-NPC overlap is affected.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Split the predicate. The per-step gate refuses any occupied active-object cell unconditionally. The BFS/workspace predicate (npc_path_route and npc_can_step_toward_floor_link_marker) keeps the npc_dynamic_obstacle_blocks cutoff.

confirmed.contract: Contact events are produced inside the schedule pass at the start of an eligible NPC's engagement invocation. Self-created adjacency waits for a later invocation, the last producer visited wins, and gated turns produce no contact.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_07.rs:3794 calls apply_town_npc_contact_event unconditionally after apply_pending_town_object_epilogue (:3829-3846), which may have skipped advance_npc_schedules. town_adjacent_event_npc (chunk_07.rs:4189-4220) is a post-pass find_map over roster order: the first adjacent eligible NPC wins. It has no check that the NPC reached AI dispatch (it does not check state or the boundary hour). It runs after NPC moves, so self-created adjacency fires on the same turn.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Record the event (kind + roster index, overwritten by each later producer) inside advance_npc_schedules at the start of the AI-dispatch engagement arm, before any step, and clear it at pass start. apply_town_npc_contact_event then consumes only that recorded event and does nothing when the pass did not run.

confirmed.contract: For AI 6/7 with dialogue other than 0xFE, linked live sprite exactly 0x70 gives arrest. Any other sprite gives the conflict outcome: actor byte >= 0x40 gives Attacked! and the NPC-conflict chain, and a lower byte clears the slot.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_07.rs:4142-4180 routes by AI value only. raises_guard_event (AI 6 only, npc_runtime.rs:470) always opens arrest, and AI 7 always runs town_alarm_sweep and returns Used. The runtime contact path has no sprite==0x70 test, no Attacked!/conflict entry and no slot-clear branch. TALK_GUARD_SPRITE 0x70 is used only by the talk paths in chunk_04.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In apply_town_npc_contact_event, after the 0xFE brush-off, branch on the linked active object's live sprite for both AI 6 and 7. 0x70 opens arrest. Otherwise, actor byte >= 0x40 prints Attacked! and enters the NPC-conflict combat chain, and a lower byte clears the NPC slot.

confirmed.contract: Boundaries need not be sorted. The active waypoint is the boundary with the smallest unsigned 8-bit hour - time[i] (the most recent past boundary), mapped through [0,1,2,1].
confirmed.evidence: tile_helpers.rs:1749-1761 waypoint_for_hour uses in_wrapping_range(t0,t1) and then (t2,t3), else 1. It is called by the walker (chunk_10.rs:793), init (npc_runtime.rs:798/825), contact (chunk_07.rs:4199), the step gate (chunk_11.rs:156) and others. For time=[8,20,12,22] at hour 13 it returns 0, where the spec gives 2. Equal boundaries always return 1. The most-recent version town_mode.rs:726 npc_schedule_waypoint_for_hour has no runtime caller, and it uses mod-24 rather than unsigned 8-bit subtraction.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Reimplement waypoint_for_hour as argmin over i of hour.wrapping_sub(time[i]) (u8), mapped through [0,1,2,1] with the first index winning ties. Alternatively delegate to a corrected npc_schedule_waypoint_for_hour.

confirmed.contract: Search goals are exactly the cells carrying the selected marker 0xC8/0xC9, and stairways are not goals. For states 4/5 the link is the nearest reachable marker cell measured by the BFS.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:1670 sets the BFS goal test to npc_floor_link_arrival_accepts(tile, marker), which also accepts 0xC4..0xC7. floor_link_marker_coordinates (:1752-1761) uses the same predicate. For states 4/5, nearest_npc_floor_link_to (:1741-1749) is a min-Manhattan-to-waypoint pick with no BFS or reachability check, and it places the NPC there directly (:1590-1601).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Use `grid[idx] == marker` as the goal test in npc_path_route_to_floor_link_marker and floor_link_marker_coordinates, and keep the stairway acceptance only in the on-floor gate and the arrival re-read. For states 4/5, choose the link by the tile-ID BFS, then re-read the tile before surfacing.

confirmed.contract: On a refused on-floor gate, the walker routes toward the link via the tile-ID search and enters queue-replay state 3. A drained queue re-enters 6/7 and ends the tick.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:1564-1579: when the gate refuses, it calls npc_path_step_to_floor_link, which takes only the first direction code (:1617-1626). It moves one cell and resets the state to 6/7 via schedule_floor_state. No move queue is installed and state 3 is never entered, so each tick re-searches under the per-tick latch, and the §7 drain-to-6/7 EndTick path is unreachable for this case.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Install the full route from npc_path_route_to_floor_link_marker into move_queue, set state NPC_STATE_REPLAY_QUEUE, and let advance_npc_replay_queue_step handle the drain-to-6/7 EndTick transition.

confirmed.contract: Only one NPC per tick may start a fresh search, and later would-be searchers are skipped. A spent budget diverts a boundary-hour NPC to the cheap arm (AI dispatch with the cached waypoint).
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:1025-1051: a state-2 NPC whose direct step failed while `searched` is set goes to npc_route_recovery_wander, a cap-zero coin-gated random step that can move the NPC. That matches neither published arm: §7 says to skip, and §6/§9.1 say the cached-waypoint cheap arm, a diverted NPC that 'stands still without aging'. The engine comment at :1037-1049 concedes this mapping is unresolved. (The settled-at-boundary case at :826-832 does use cached_wp correctly.)
confirmed.fix_sketch: When the latch is spent for a state-2 NPC, do not call the recovery stepper. Either skip the slot (§7) or route it to the cached-waypoint AI dispatch (§6 cheap arm); ask the spec owner which one applies to an in-flight state-2 NPC.

confirmed.contract: Each BFS iteration tries the four cardinal directions in cyclic order over codes 1=W, 2=S, 3=E, 4=N, so ties break by that order.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:1491 and :1654 iterate map_decoders.rs:307 neighbors(), which yields W, E, N, S. That is not a rotation of the W,S,E,N cycle, so equal-length routes resolve differently. The spec implies, but does not state explicitly, that the cycle starts from the dequeued cell's high-nibble 'current direction'. The engine fails under any rotation.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Replace neighbors() in both NPC BFS routines with an iterator over direction codes 1..4 in cyclic order, starting from the dequeued cell's inbound code (start cell seeded with 4=north). Ask the spec owner to confirm the exact rotation start.

confirmed.contract: Loading in town restores the schedule table, runtime block, move queues, cursors and stuck counters verbatim. The first tick continues the saved route without recomputing from the hour or snapping.
confirmed.evidence: chunk_10.rs:471-509 builds every NPC via RuntimeNpc::from_slot(slot, hour) (npc_runtime.rs:797-814), which sets state idle, cached_wp from the hour, an empty queue, stuck 0, and hour-waypoint coordinates for off-floor NPCs. Only the on-floor x/y come from the restored active objects, paired by type and floor (:590-620). npc_band.rs:378 read_npc_band exists but has no caller in the runtime load path. The comments at :463-470 and :576-580 concede this.
confirmed.fix_sketch: On a preserving town load, decode the 0x07B4..0x105F band with read_npc_band and use those RuntimeNpc records (state, cached_wp, position, queue, cursor, stuck counter, linked slot) instead of from_slot plus type/floor pairing.

ambiguous.contract: For a keyboard-driven combatant the asleep arm comes after the banner, and a 0..255 < 16 draw wakes the sleeper before `Zzzzz...` prints.
ambiguous.evidence: §8.1 (combat.md:2254-2255) says '1-in-256 draw below sixteen wakes the sleeper before Zzzzz... prints'. §6.2 (combat.md:1271-1278) says the dispatch of any slot still carrying 0x08 rolls inclusive 0..16 and wakes on 16, and a woken actor does not continue 'into the normal action parser or monster action path'. The engine (combat_frame.rs:8076-8091; combat_actor.rs:209-211) implements §6.2 for all slots and prints the banner and Zzzzz before the roll. The two sections give different draws for what may be the same dispatch. §8.1 also does not say whether a woken keyboard sleeper then reads a command, or whether it prints anything in place of Zzzzz.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Ask the spec to reconcile §6.2 and §8.1: whether the prompted path uses a separate 0..255<16 draw instead of the 0..16==16 one, and what a woken prompted actor does next. Then move the roll ahead of the Zzzzz print for prompted slots.

ambiguous.contract: Up is also offered on a gear-marked cell when the party carries climbing gear. A gear-marked cell with neither direction gives `Klimb-\nWith What?\n`. `Failed!` never appears on the K route.
ambiguous.evidence: The spec never publishes which raw bit is the climbable-with-equipment mark, and 8.1 says the gear-byte identification is 'probable, not established'. The gear arm and DUNGEON_KLIMB_WITH_WHAT_REFUSAL (commands.rs:1872, unused) cannot be wired without guessing. The K route itself (chunk_08.rs:1003-1021) never reaches `Failed!`. That line comes only from the engine-only '<'/'>' keys (chunk_02.rs:179-184) via climb_dungeon chunk_08.rs:1219-1238. Those keys are an engine invention rather than a K-route violation, but they are worth removing.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Ask for the gear-mark bit to be published. Meanwhile, drop or route the '<'/'>' dungeon arms so the Failed!/CastFailure path is unreachable outside the Up/Down spells.

ambiguous.section: 6.4 Two flavour-conditional extras (chamber-name banner, flavour-3 flourish)
ambiguous.contract: A 0xB? wall ahead with a non-zero low nibble prints the per-dungeon chamber-name banner in the runic font. A 0xC? wall ahead in a flavour-3 dungeon draws four bright strokes on about a 1-in-16 roll.
ambiguous.evidence: The engine has neither feature (no banner or flourish code; grep for chamber/LOST SOULS/MOTHER LODE in crates/ finds nothing). The spec does not publish what is needed to build them without guessing. Each banner is 'a multi-line block positioned at its own origin', but the line breaks, origins and per-dungeon index-to-banner table are not given. The NG/EE glyph readings are only 'probable', whether the banner clears itself is 'not traced', and the flourish's stroke coordinates and pen are given only as 'near the vanishing point' and 'roughly one-in-sixteen'.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Ask the spec owner to publish the per-dungeon banner index table, the origins and line layout, and the flourish stroke geometry, pen and exact roll.

ambiguous.contract: The ambush arena painter fills with the corridor byte and stamps the outline, corner markers, centre icon and per-side openings (passable: 7 cells, wall: sealed, door: 5 cells) keyed on the adjoining dungeon cells.
ambiguous.evidence: The engine fills only (combat_arena.rs:278-327) and stamps the chest icon alone (combat_setup.rs:1343-1347). However, the spec does not publish the outline byte, the wall-line position, the corner-marker bytes, the non-chest centre-icon bytes or the carve positions. It also flags its own limits: the painter was 'read only through about half its length' and the filler byte is identified 'by inference'. The engine comment notes the unpublished icon bytes.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Ask for the outline, corner and icon byte values and the carve coordinates. Then add an adjoining-cell input to synthesise_dungeon_ambush and stamp the per-side treatment.

ambiguous.section: §8 Special/marquee effects (Negate Time) and §5.1 closing paragraph
ambiguous.contract: An Tym scans for a magic-absorption sentinel; if present it prints `Magic absorbed!` then `Failed!` and does not install `T`.
ambiguous.evidence: The spec never defines what the 'magic-absorption sentinel' is, where it lives or what sets it (magic.md:1407, 1429; audio.md:670 calls it 'an absorbing actor'). The engine's cast_time_stop (chunk_03.rs:6144-6183) handles only the scene Absorbed! gate and notes no absorbing actor is modelled. It cannot be implemented without guessing the sentinel's identity.

ambiguous.contract: The ambient shrine/flame tick plays 3000 Hz for 3 units on residue 0 of its eight-phase counter and 2000 Hz on residue 4. The same residues select the loud envelope in the lava/shrine branch.
ambiguous.evidence: The spec gives the tone recipes and residues (audio.md:992, :1080-1082; time.md:444-450) but never says what makes the ambient tick reach its tone or envelope arm: which tiles near the party, the radius, or which terrain counts as lava/shrine. audio.md:1935 says only 'keyed on nearby tiles'. audio.md 8.3.2 (:1274-1280) and 11 (:2184) list how often it fires during prompts, and its other entry points, as unresolved. OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:197/206 keep its contribution unpriced. The engine (clock.rs:111-131; chunk_09.rs:3556) models only the counter and countdown decay that time.md fully specifies. Emitting the tone needs a trigger predicate the spec does not publish.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Ask for a spec addition that defines the ambient tick's tile/proximity predicate and its envelope parameters. Then add an AmbientTick SoundEffect, driven from tick_ambient_audio_repeats on residues 0 and 4.

ambiguous.contract: After the circle rumble, Sleep/Poison Wind/Death Wind/Flame Wind run a 21x21 raster in which each drawn cell retunes the speaker to a pseudorandom 100..10,000 Hz pitch, with one tone stop after the raster.
ambiguous.evidence: audio.md:773-776 lists the raster tone's rate as unresolved: 'entirely a function of the cell-draw cost ... cannot be published as a frequency-versus-time curve'. The spec also does not say which PRNG supplies the pitches, or whether undrawn cells retune. Without a per-cell duration the effect has no defined length or sound, so any emitted program would invent its timing. The engine deliberately emits only CircleRumbleLead (/home/gamedev/worktrees/u5-engine/audit-6df53be7/crates/u5-runtime/src/combat_frame.rs:5544-5551) and cites that text.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: Once the spec publishes a cell-draw rate (or a capture), add a MassTargetRaster SoundEffect: 441 sustained retunes at uniform pitches in 100..10000 Hz from a non-gameplay jitter source, then one stop, emitted after CircleRumbleLead.

ambiguous.section: 5 (hour-gated part of status pass) and 11 (0x02DA row)
ambiguous.contract: The status pass's food/starvation hour gate uses the shared 0x02DA snapshot, which the time-advancing cleanup also writes, so hours crossed in camp or combat never spend food.
ambiguous.evidence: time.md:160-178 says the pass 'keeps its own previous-hour snapshot' and updates it after the branch. The engine follows that literally with a separate status_pass_previous_hour (chunk_09.rs:3313-3317). But time.md:432, saved-gam.md:186 and RETRACTIONS R338 say 0x02DA is written by both the cleanup and the party-upkeep pass, which suggests one shared byte. The two readings give different food results after a camp or combat that crosses 06/12/18, and the spec does not say which one the gate reads.

ambiguous.contract: v1 baseline is the enhanced-display colour space: index 6 renders dark yellow; brown at index 6 is legitimate only as a frontend-offered period-monitor emulation mode.
ambiguous.evidence: Runtime baseline is enhanced: crates/u5-runtime/src/graphics.rs:255 DISPLAY_MODEL = MonitorModel::Enhanced, with EGA_PALETTE_RGB at :257. The Bevy frontend (crates/u5-bevy/src/lib.rs:228-246) deliberately applies MonitorModel::Period200Line as a display model over the same shipped register values, with no toggle. The spec says implementations targeting the enhanced space 'should' render dark yellow, and also that 'A frontend offering a period-monitor emulation mode may legitimately show brown there, and that is a display model, not a palette change'. It never says whether the emulation must be optional or whether the shipped graphical client must default to the enhanced model. The frontend is exactly the 'display model, not a palette change' case the spec allows, and the per-index mapping stays consistent, which is the stated semantic contract. Whether a frontend that only offers period mode conforms is a judgement the text does not settle.
ambiguous.fix_sketch: If the user or spec settles that the default must be enhanced: make the Bevy palette selectable at runtime (setting, CLI flag or key) with MonitorModel::Enhanced as the default, keeping Period200Line as an opt-in emulation mode.

ambiguous.contract: A successful summon installs the actor two cells north and plays the appearance line with the long warble and the fade-in effect. No slot-number diagnostics.
ambiguous.evidence: The engine does print an invented diagnostic with the slot number (chunk_07.rs:1370-1378) and emits no sound or fade, so it does not conform.
